open.speaker: clerk
lines: Couple from Ohio checked out at three in the morning. Said something tapped on their window.
I don't go up there now.

passives.line: He doesn't go up there. His eyes do. Every few seconds, to the ceiling, to the exact spot.
Three in the morning, and they checked out rather than ran. Somebody stood at this counter and paid. He talked to them. He is leaving that part out.
Second floor, no balcony. Whatever taps on a window it cannot stand under is standing on nothing, and comfortable there.

static.line: The key's in his shirt pocket. Left side. He won't stop you. He wants you to take it so it isn't his any more.

options.text: They paid before they left. What did they say to you?
Your register. Anyone else check in that week? Cash, no plates?
Three a.m. checkouts. You get a lot of those?

heard.speaker: clerk
lines: ...I heard the couple. Running on the walk. I heard the ice machine. I heard the ice machine stop.
Ice machine don't stop. I don't know what I heard.
You don't have to know. You just have to say it.

paid.speaker: clerk
lines: The wife paid. Husband wouldn't come in off the walk. She said, 'It wasn't a branch,' and I hadn't said branch. Nobody had said branch.
She tipped. Nobody tips a motel. Twenty dollars, on the counter, and she said, 'Don't go up till it's light.'

ledger.speaker: clerk
lines: Two men. Room 9. Paid a week up front in new bills and never slept in the bed; maid says the bed's made the way she made it.
Car with no plates. Parks nose out, lights off. Some nights the engine's running and nobody's in it.

ledger_fail.speaker: clerk
lines: Register's private. I don't read it to anybody with a notebook.
You want names, the Lowe Hotel keeps a book on the counter in plain sight and a night clerk who'll read it to you for a cup of coffee.

nights.speaker: clerk
lines: Since Thursday? Four. Four in a week, in February, when I'd be lucky to have four rooms let.
All second floor. All said tapping. None of 'em knew each other. I stopped putting people up there Saturday.
Four. That's a pattern, not a story. Patterns are better.

nights_fail.speaker: clerk
lines: Rooms are twenty-two a night. Ground floor only. Checkout's eleven.

silent.speaker: clerk
lines: You're in 6. Ground floor. I put you on the ground floor on purpose and I'd take it as a kindness if you didn't ask to be moved.

hub.speaker: clerk
lines: Anything else. I'm here all night. That's the job.

options.text: What did you see on the roof, the night you stopped going up?
Get some sleep if you can.

roofline.speaker: clerk
lines: ...Saturday. I went up with the master to check 14 after the fourth couple. Got to the top of the stairs.
Two lights on the roofline. Red, like a car backing up. On the roof. There's no road on the roof.
They turned. Together. The way eyes do. I came down the stairs and I have not been up since and I would like you to not ask me again.

roofline_fail.speaker: clerk
lines: I didn't see anything. I'm not a witness. I'm the night clerk.
Rooms are twenty-two a night. Checkout's eleven. The office is closed.
He saw something. And now he'll never say what, not to us.

passives.line: You asked for the thing he could not afford to give, and he paid you with the price list instead. That door is shut for good.
